Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
643 PM EST Sat Nov 7 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 123 PM EST Saturday...

Rain chances and amounts have been cut along the international 
border for today.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 123 PM EST Saturday...

1. Weather will be steady-state with cool, showery conditions.

2. Remaining unsettled mid week, then trending cooler by next 
weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 123 PM EST Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: We'll be in a bit of a rinse-repeat pattern through at 
least Tuesday. Two upper lows will merge early this week, and 
patches of embedded moisture will result in showery conditions. 
There will be lulls in activity, though, with the greatest chances 
of limited shower activity Sunday afternoon and Tuesday morning. 
During the day on Tuesday, a shortwave ridge will build ahead of an 
incoming low that will open into a trough as it shifts east-
southeast. This will result in flattened 500mb heights with a trend 
towards decreasing heading into the middle of next week. Forecast 
high temperatures will be in the mid-40s to mid-50s, and overnight 
lows will range near 30 to near 40 for the next 3-4 days.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Cyclonic flow centered over eastern Canada will swing a 
couple shortwaves through northern New York and Vermont next mid 
week. The first is modeled to swing through on Tuesday night, 
resulting in chance of precipitation 30-60%, locally 55-85% across 
the northern Greens. As temperatures fall into the upper 20s to mid 
30s, some of the higher elevations could see some snow mixing in 
with the rain early Wednesday morning. Depending on the strength of 
high pressure to our south, there's the chance for additional 
showers during the daytime Wednesday hours as well (15-45% chance), 
though most spots should see temperatures warm into the 40s and 
lower 50s that afternoon, resulting in mainly rain. Model 
consensus really falls apart by Wednesday night, but the main 
agreements relate to brief weak ridging over the area into 
Thursday, then a deep trough or closed low developing over the 
midwest towards Friday. Based on this, chances for precip run 
10-40% for the late week accompanied by highs upper 30s to near 
50 F and lows in the teens to near 30 F. Models are suggesting a
coastal storm could set up next weekend to bring more steady 
precipitation to the region, but the details are not clear that 
far out.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 00Z Monday...Low ceilings, rain, and mist will persist
overnight, resulting in MVFR, IFR, and LIFR conditions through
14Z Sunday. Highest chance of persistent LIFR ceilings will 
remain at KMPV, KRUT, and KSLK, where ceilings are observed 
ceilings are 300 to 400 ft AGL and no improvement is expected 
until late morning Sunday. Other TAF sites are starting off the
TAF period with mainly MVFR ceilings, though lowering of 
ceilings to IFR with occasional periods of LIFR is expected 
during the overnight hours. Visibilities will also decrease at 
times at all TAF sites overnight due to periods of rain and 
mist, though ceilings will be the main factor driving the lowest
flight conditions. 

Showers will scatter out and ceilings will slowly lift after
14Z. However, improvement will be slow, especially at higher
elevation TAF sites where IFR conditions could persist into the
early afternoon. By late afternoon and evening Sunday, ceilings
areawide will lift to MVFR/VFR levels. 

Winds will remain from the north generally 6-12 knots, with some
occasional gusts 15 to 18 knots. 

Outlook...

Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Monday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Monday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance RA.
Tuesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance RA.
Veterans Day: Mainly MVFR, with local VFR possible. Chance RA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance SN,
Slight chance RA.
Thursday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight chance RA.

&&

.MARINE...
Northwest winds are expected to increase overnight, reaching around 
15-25 knots for the broad and southern waters of Lake Champlain by 
about midnight. Winds will begin to subside before sunrise, trending 
towards 10-20 by morning and continuing into Sunday afternoon. Waves 
across the broad and southern waters will likely range between 2 to 
4 feet overnight into early Sunday morning.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
